svg.aria-label: FlashAttention computes the same attention but never writes the N by N score matrix. Q, K, V and the output O live in HBM, which is big and slow, and there are no N by N scores there. Q is cut into row blocks and K and V into blocks along the sequence. One Q block is loaded once into the small fast on-chip SRAM and stays there while K and V blocks stream through one by one. For each pair the score tile S_ij is computed in SRAM, folded into the output accumulator o with its running max m and running sum l, and thrown away. Only O goes back to HBM. On the right, the online softmax for one query row with scores 1, 3 in block 1 and 5, 2 in block 2: after block 1, m is 3 and l is e to the -2 plus e to the 0, about 1.14, and o is the sum of e to the (s minus m) times v. Block 2 has a bigger max, m prime 5, so the old l and o are rescaled by e to the (m minus m prime) and the new block is added: l becomes 1.14 times e to the -2 plus 1.05, about 1.20. After the last block O is o divided by l, the exact softmax. On newer GPUs the matmuls got so fast that exp and rescaling start to dominate, which FlashAttention-4 targets.
